name: Joseph Klaits
specialization: Psychological approach to prosecution; gender and sexuality in witch-hunting; French and Central European cases

major_works.title: Servants of Satan: The Age of the Witch Hunts
major_works.significance: Psychological approach to prosecution dynamics; analysis of gender and sexuality in demonological ideology; French and Central European case focus

core_argument: Witch prosecutions were driven by psychological dynamics including fear of female sexuality and reproductive power, combined with clerical male anxiety about women's bodies. The psychological content of witch confessions — which focus heavily on diabolical sexual intercourse, bodily harm, and disruption of fertility — reveals deep cultural anxieties that motivated accusers and judges alike.

methodological_approach.primary_materials: Trial records and confessional narratives from France and Central Europe; demonological texts emphasizing sexual and bodily themes
methodological_approach.analysis_target: Psychological content of witch confessions; gender and sexuality in prosecution patterns; role of clerical male psychology in persecution
methodological_approach.evidence_type: Psycho-historical analysis of confession content; comparative case study approach
methodological_approach.explanatory_level: Psychological and cultural: gendered anxieties and clerical psychosexual dynamics as driving forces

key_contributions.claim: The emphasis on sexual intercourse with the devil in witch confessions reflects clerical male anxiety about female sexuality, projected onto accused women through leading questions and torture
key_contributions.implication: The sexual content of demonology was not incidental but reflected the psychology of those conducting prosecutions

key_contributions.claim: Fear of harm to crops, cattle, children, and reproductive capacity was the core content of maleficium charges, reflecting deep anxieties about subsistence and family survival
key_contributions.implication: Witchcraft accusations were rooted in concrete economic and bodily fears, not merely theological abstraction

reception_and_critique.major_influences: Psychohistory; social history of gender; feminist historiography
criticisms: Psychohistorical approach vulnerable to same anachronism objections as other psychoanalytic approaches
Less empirically grounded than regional specialists like Midelfort or Briggs
Synthesis work rather than primary archival research

historiographical_significance: Klaits provided an accessible synthesis of psychological and gender approaches to witch-hunting that helped bring these perspectives to students and non-specialist audiences. His emphasis on sexuality and fertility as core psychological drivers of prosecution anticipated more sophisticated treatments by Roper and others. His textbook synthesis served an important pedagogical function in establishing gender as a central analytical category.
source_method: Published scholarship and critical historiographical reconstruction
